Hon'ble Vinod Diwakar,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, Shri R.K. Jaiswal, learned counsel for the respondent,
and perused the record.

2. The instant writ petition is preferred with the prayer to quash the order dated 28.05.2025 passed by Special Land Acquisition Officer, Varansi-respondent no.2 in a proceeding under Section 3H(3)
National Highway Act 1956, by which the objection of the petitioners has been rejected and a direction is issued to pay adequate compensation to the parties having a stake in the land/property.

entities.text: Brijraj Singh And 6 Others vs Executive Engineer National Highway
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
While passing the order impugned, respondent no.2 has decided/rejected the objection of the petitioners in a proceeding under Section 3H(3) of National Highway Act, 1956 and directed to ensure compensation to the land owners, on the basis of share (Hissafat) dated 05.10.2024 and the report of Sub Division Magistrate, Rajatalab dated 24.02.2025, by means of reasoned and speaking order with a rider that, in the interest of justice, an agreement be taken from the persons, who would receive compensation, to the effect that in case a competent court decided ownership against them,
they would repay the compensation alongwith interest.
The order impugned not only decides the objection of the petitioners but also provides protection to them in case they succeed in the competent court.

4. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the records, we do not find any infirmity or illegality in the order impugned, which requires interference under Article 226 of the Constitution of India.
However, it is always open for the petitioners to press the relief before the Competent Court.
5. The writ petition is disposed of.
